newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee consumers inactive despite tightness.
newsitem.headline: German coffee consumers inactive despite tightness.

text.p: German coffee roasters reduced their buying activity in tight nearby markets although last week's falls in futures would have offered savings in outright prices, traders said on Monday.
"Consumers took some cover in cold early summer markets, then they were surprised by the hot August. Now physical buying's off again as cover remains comfortable," one said.
"Roastings in August were not as high as expected."
New York arabica futures were closed for a public holiday on Monday and London robustas were mixed in thin trades.
The September open interest in New York has declined, but still equals 320,000 bags of coffee, with Exchange warehouses only holding just under 40,000 bags.
"It's still uncomfortable for the shorts," one trader said.
He added fears persisted that the New York September/December switch, currently at 10.1 cents, could be rolled forward into December/March, where the gap at Friday's close was just 5.8.
But there was less urgency in dealings than in recent weeks.
Importers reported some demand for October-February Brazils and newly-auctioned Kenyan fly crop to replace Colombians, where differentials remained high and material tight.
More Centralamerican coffees were on offer, with new crops starting early and differentials were seen falling.
Competitive robusta offers for nearby shipments were ignored, but buyers lined up for January onwards.
Brazils cost $121 per 50 kg fob and Colombia Excelso coffee $150 for October/November $150, Kenyans $153, and Indonesia cif robustas for October $71. All coffees were off $3 on the week.
